current.critique: The three steps done are real: a general magnet field, Biot-Savart over wound turns and a crane that drops spikes on a friend are honest clips, and they show the solver is not a rig. But the road has grown to 17 steps and it wanders. Lightning-made lodestones, iron-sand putting and a fire you fight are each fine toys, but none brings the first motor closer, and the circuit solver, the one thing every later step needs, still sits untouched in the middle. The minute-to-minute play while the coil is wound is still not stated, and electricity sandboxes are well-trodden, so memorable rests entirely on the fields being real.

goals.title: From beach stones to an electric cart
goals.critique: This is the current goal with an end you can point at, and a road in the right order: circuit, cell, the powered crane, the hand-fitted motor, the generator on the wheel, then the frame and the cart. Each step is a toy on its own, and the side trips are cut. 'Too few cells and it crawls up the dune, a loose brush makes it stutter' tells the player what to change next, and the runaway down the far side with three friends aboard is a clip people would send. The weak side: it is almost word for word the human's own closing example, so nobody is surprised, and hand-built vehicles that drive by their parts are Besiege and Scrap Mechanic ground. Narrowing to one machine brings back the convergence fault of the wing rounds, because once the cart climbs the hill the pull is gone unless the parts keep feeding other builds. Rolling contact on sand, brush commutation and the regenerative braking step are the places where a scripted torque or a drive-force fudge would most easily slip in.
